title: Spreadsheets in practice: formulas, filters and charts

videos.script: Three lessons ago a spreadsheet was a model: a cell holds a value and a formula computes one. This one is how to build one that somebody else can check. {{check}} That sounds like tidiness and it is not. A spreadsheet is the only document in this course that produces a number somebody will act on, and it is the only one with no way to tell a correct number from a confident one. A wrong total does not look wrong. {{wrong}} So almost everything here is one idea: make the sheet say what it assumes. Inputs in one place, calculations in another, no number typed inside a formula, and a column whose only job is to check the other columns. {{idea}} Then the three things that turn a table into an answer — filters, lookups, and the pivot table, which is the highest-leverage feature in this entire course. {{tools}} And charts, where the one rule is that the picture must not say something the numbers do not.
